UPSTREAM: ASoC: dapm: Fix NULL pointer deference on CODEC to CODEC DAIs Commit a655de808cbde ("ASoC: core: Allow topology to override machine driver FE DAI link config.") caused soc_dai_hw_params to be come dependent on the substream private_data being set with a pointer to the snd_soc_pcm_runtime. Currently, CODEC to CODEC links don't set this, which causes a NULL pointer dereference: [<4069de54>] (soc_dai_hw_params) from [<40694b68>] (snd_soc_dai_link_event+0x1a0/0x380) Since the ASoC core in general assumes that the substream private_data will be set to a pointer to the snd_soc_pcm_runtime, update the CODEC to CODEC links to respect this. UPSTREAM: ASoC: dpcm: Properly initialise hw->rate_max If the CPU DAI does not initialise rate_max, say if using using KNOT or CONTINUOUS, then the rate_max field will be initialised to 0. A value of zero in the rate_max field of the hardware runtime will cause the sound card to support no sample rates at all. Obviously this is not desired, just a different mechanism is being used to apply the constraints. As such update the setting of rate_max in dpcm_init_runtime_hw to be consistent with the non-DPCM cases and set rate_max to UINT_MAX if nothing is defined on the CPU DAI. Signed-off-by: Charles Keepax <ckeepax@opensource.cirrus.com> Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit e33ffbd9cd39da09831ce62c11025d830bf78d9e) Signed-off-by: Samaga Prasanna Krishna <samaga.krishna@intel.corp-partner.google.com> BUG=b:110025789 TEST=Test Audio use cases with full SOF 0.6 rebase release series applied. main: add panic hook that redirects to syslog The default panic hook prints panic information and a backtrace to stderr, where it gets dropped into /dev/null in the typical crostini context. This change adds a panic hook that will call the default panic hook with stderr redirected to a pipe, which will then get forwarded to syslog. The new hook also forces an abort at the end to ensure the crash reporter sees the panicked crosvm process, which will generate a minidump for later debugging. init: chromeos_startup: make clobbering a little more robust If you start a dev<->verified mode transition and reboot in the middle, the next power up will trigger a powerwash which can be confusing to users. This is because we [re]use the RESET_FILE to pass args to the clobber function, and those files don't get wiped until the stateful clobbering finishes. Instead, lets use normal shell variables to hold things. This shouldn't impact system security as the other nvram settings/stateful files will still handle the transition correctly if a reboot happens. cros_generate_update_payload: Use new paygen library This is where things getting interesting. Basically this patch starts calling the chromite's paygen library instead of directly calling delta_generator. This makes everything much cleaner and extensible. Added these flags: --check: Verifies the integrity of the payload. --work_dir: This was mistakenly removed in the past. Added it back. Removed a lot of unused and unnecessary flags. Also changed the partition_lib API a bit to accommodate for optionally truncating the root partition. With this change the run time of cros_generate_update_payload increases by about 20~30 seconds. The reason being is an added extra copy that happens either from the cache to a temporary tgt_image.bin file. It might not be a good idea to get rid of that extra copy because if the file changes in the middle, the paygen can get screwed up. So we might better be safe than sorry!! I think the value we gain from this change from software engineering POV is much higher than the slight loss in the performance. We could potentially improve this by smarter caching logic in the future. BUG=chromium:862679 TEST=cros flash inside and outside chroot TEST=unittests TEST=payload-tryjob Change-Id: I66a02df093ffb65f2797904572c6b87fb76d782d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1369108 Commit-Ready: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Tested-by: Amin Hassani <ahassani@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Don Garrett <dgarrett@chromium.org>

ec3po_interface.py: Suppress EPIPE when writing to shutdown pipes. EC3PO uses pipes to ask the console and interpreter threads to shutdown. Those threads could potentially exit first, even just from SIGINT / KeyboardInterrupt, and in most such scenarios they will close() the read side of the shutdown pipes. BUG=b:79684405,chromium:925243 TEST=No tracebacks, hangs, or logged errors when shutting down with Servo v4 (CCD), Servo Micro, and Servo v4 + Servo Micro. I tested use of (ec|servo_(v4|micro))_uart_pty with each, and tested telling servod to quit via SIGINT (ctrl+c) and SIGTERM with each. I also edited ec3po/console.py (not in this patch) to close shutdown_pipe early in order to forcibly reproduce the crbug:925243 problem. With that change and without this patch, the same traceback occurred upon SIGINT, and servod hung until receiving another signal. With this patch, servod shut down cleanly, both from SIGINT and SIGTERM. Change-Id: I52834f8594a7013586cf2027f663b8297520ffd9 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1450513 Reviewed-by: Aseda Aboagye <aaboagye@chromium.org>

shill: Distinguish between an unknown failure and no failure at all Prior to this CL, kFailureUnknown was used to represent both an unknown failure and for no failure. This is incovenient for a number of reasons, and led to logs indicating unknown failure when completely normal control flow occurs. This change adds kFailureNone to be used as the value representing no failure. kFailureUnknown is moved to a different value such that kFailureNone may be value 0. While this affects existing metrics, the metrics we have on kFailureUnknown are mostly useless, as we cannot distinguish between real failures and no failures anyways. Note that for cellular, any disconnects from PPP still result in setting the failure to kFailureUnknown, even if the disconnect is not the result of any failure. Changing this behavior requires either modifying how shill interacts with pppd through the PPP class or assuming that a PPP disconnect after successful authentication is intentional. A very similar CL was originally written by @semenzato many moons ago: https://android-review.googlesource.com/c/platform/system/connectivity/shill/+/209433 BUG=chromium:596197 TEST=- Normal state changes in shill are now logged without indicating an unknown failure, while state changes due to actual failures do show a failure. - All unit tests are passing.
